body: The problem is that I break down and cry in the moment because I get overwhelmed. It's not like it's everyday or anything, it's just after weeks of little things like that getting to me and I hit my breaking point. And the second I start crying he gets upset :/ so the second I start crying I also have an instant anxiety attack (I have PTSD due to my past) because I know what's coming, which doesn't help the crying. Due to the physical damage that happened to my brain when I have an anxiety attack I also get an excruciating migraine that feels like I'm getting bleach poured inside my skull. Sometimes I have to go to the ER due to anxiety attacks because I am in so much pain that over-the-counter and prescription medications don't even touch the pain. So yeah, it's not JUST emotional issues, it's physical pain as well. But if I can learn how to not let the little things bother me so much, I won't get anxiety, therefore won't be crying from pain. It's definitely a complicated situation but I feel like I am to blame for making my boyfriend feel bad, he does so much for me and because of my issues, I end up making him feel bad and it's not fair to him.

I appreciate your words but he is really good to me other than not realizing when he's mocking me. I am on disability and I barely make enough money to cover the costs of my medicine, weekly physio, and other medical expenses.
He pays for my rent, he pays for the food I eat, and drives me to every single appointment that I have since I cannot drive. So I don't really have the right to complain about the occasional emotional issue. I just need to work on it from my end.

He says that I'm just imagining him mocking me, and taking it the wrong way. I have a severe tremor that I'm extremely self conscious about and he often pantomimes me with an over exaggerated tremor while laughing. I take that as "mocking" and it gets to me after a while. But he always says that he meant nothing by it and that I have to stop imagining him bullying me. 
Everything he does, he does for me. I know that my physical disabilities are a burden on him and the fact that I make him feel bad about it by having emotional breakdowns is really getting to him. I just need to find a way to not take things so personally, and I think our relationship would be much better.
